title: When the Cotton Stopped, Robert Owen Kept Paying New Lanark
conflicts: All sources follow Owen's own date of 1806, although the US Embargo Act was December 1807 and ran over a year; the story says 'as Owen dated it' and does not name the act. The cost is Owen's own 'more than seven thousand pounds' (Lloyd Jones: 'seven thousand pounds', 'nearly four months'; Podmore, museum and Undiscovered Scotland give four months, no sum); attributed to Owen. Owen writes as if he decided alone; Podmore says he persuaded his partners; Podmore's version is attributed to Podmore. Wikipedia (1818) and Undiscovered Scotland (1816) disagree on the Institute's opening, so it is not dated.
notes: Owen's autobiography is cited from the 1920 Bell reprint of the 1857-58 text on the Internet Archive. Funding 'mixed': partners' capital plus twenty-year vendor instalments to Dale. Quote stance: affirms.
